# College tech fest manager

Manage events with their registrations, volunteers and sponsors.

**registrations**: student_name (string), college (string), email (string), phone (string), team_name (string), status (Registered / Checked in / Cancelled). Operations: list, create, update, delete. Belongs to events. Actions: check_in (status = Checked in), cancel (status = Cancelled).
**volunteers**: name (string), phone (string), role (Coordinator / Helper / Tech support), shift (Morning / Afternoon / Evening). Operations: list, create, update, delete. Belongs to events.
**sponsors**: company_name (string), contact_person (string), amount (number), status (Pledged / Paid). Operations: list, create, update, delete. Belongs to events. Actions: mark_paid (status = Paid).

Features:
- Add, edit and delete events
- Add, edit and delete registrations
- Add, edit and delete volunteers
- Add, edit and delete sponsors
- Filter lists by status or category
- Search by name
- Dashboard with totals and charts
Contract for events and registrations and volunteers and sponsors built from the spec: nested lists, vote actions, sort

+# Architecture
+
+**Goal:** Build a college tech fest manager: events have name, category Coding/Robotics/Gaming/Quiz/Workshop, venue, date, start time, capacity and entry fee in rupees. Each event has many registrations: student name, college, email, phone, team name and status Registered/Checked in/Cancelled; actions: check in and cancel. Each event has many volunteers: name, phone, role Coordinator/Helper/Tech support and shift Morning/Afternoon/Evening. Each event has many sponsors: company name, contact person, amount in rupees and status Pledged/Paid; action: mark paid. Show total registrations, total sponsorship received, registrations per event, filter registrations by status and events by category, search events by name, edit and delete everything.
+
+**Preset:** fastapi-vanilla
+
+4 SQLite tables (events and registrations and volunteers and sponsors) with one database module each; every module's schema creates all tables. FastAPI routers, one per resource. Counters are owned by the server and change only through action endpoints; lists are ordered by the query field sort. A multi-page app (dashboard, a page per resource, a detail page) is served from static/.
+
+## Product spec
+
+### College tech fest manager
+
+Manage events with their registrations, volunteers and sponsors.
+
+**events**: name (string), category (Coding / Robotics / Gaming / Quiz / Workshop), venue (string), date (string), start_time (string), capacity (integer), entry_fee (number). Operations: list, create, update, delete.
+**registrations**: student_name (string), college (string), email (string), phone (string), team_name (string), status (Registered / Checked in / Cancelled). Operations: list, create, update, delete. Belongs to events. Actions: check_in (status = Checked in), cancel (status = Cancelled).
+**volunteers**: name (string), phone (string), role (Coordinator / Helper / Tech support), shift (Morning / Afternoon / Evening). Operations: list, create, update, delete. Belongs to events.
+**sponsors**: company_name (string), contact_person (string), amount (number), status (Pledged / Paid). Operations: list, create, update, delete. Belongs to events. Actions: mark_paid (status = Paid).
+
+Features:
+- Add, edit and delete events
+- Add, edit and delete registrations
+- Add, edit and delete volunteers
+- Add, edit and delete sponsors
+- Filter lists by status or category
+- Search by name
+- Dashboard with totals and charts
+
+## Endpoints
+- `GET /api/events`: List all events
+- `POST /api/events`: Add a event
+- `PUT /api/events/{id}`: Edit one event
+- `DELETE /api/events/{id}`: Delete one event and its registrations, volunteers, sponsors
+- `GET /api/events/{event_id}/registrations`: List the registrations of one event
+- `POST /api/events/{event_id}/registrations`: Add a registration to a event Answers 409 when: Email already exists; Event is full.
+- `PUT /api/registrations/{id}`: Edit one registration Answers 409 when: Email already exists; That status change is not allowed.
+- `DELETE /api/registrations/{id}`: Delete one registration
+- `POST /api/registrations/{id}/check_in`: Check in one registration: sets status to Checked in and return the updated registration Answers 409 when: That status change is not allowed.
+- `POST /api/registrations/{id}/cancel`: Cancel one registration: sets status to Cancelled and return the updated registration Answers 409 when: That status change is not allowed.
+- `GET /api/events/{event_id}/volunteers`: List the volunteers of one event
+- `POST /api/events/{event_id}/volunteers`: Add a volunteer to a event
+- `PUT /api/volunteers/{id}`: Edit one volunteer
+- `DELETE /api/volunteers/{id}`: Delete one volunteer
+- `GET /api/events/{event_id}/sponsors`: List the sponsors of one event
+- `POST /api/events/{event_id}/sponsors`: Add a sponsor to a event
+- `PUT /api/sponsors/{id}`: Edit one sponsor Answers 409 when: That status change is not allowed.
+- `DELETE /api/sponsors/{id}`: Delete one sponsor
+- `POST /api/sponsors/{id}/mark_paid`: Mark paid one sponsor: sets status to Paid and return the updated sponsor Answers 409 when: That status change is not allowed.
+
+## Web page must
+- Form to add a event with name, category, venue, date, start time, capacity, entry fee
+- Edit and Delete buttons on every event
+- Form to add a registration with student name, college, email, phone, team name, status (inside the open parent)
+- Click a event (Comments button) to open its registrations with a form to add one
+- A Check in button on every registration that sets its status to Checked in
+- A Cancel button on every registration that sets its status to Cancelled
+- Edit and Delete buttons on every registration
+- Form to add a volunteer with name, phone, role, shift (inside the open parent)

+# Database schema
+
+SQLite. Connections come from `database.connection.get_conn()` (a `sqlite3.Row` factory).
+
+## Table `events`
+
+- `id` INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT
+- `name` TEXT NOT NULL
+- `category` TEXT NOT NULL
+- `venue` TEXT NOT NULL
+- `date` TEXT NOT NULL
+- `start_time` TEXT NOT NULL
+- `capacity` INTEGER NOT NULL
+- `entry_fee` REAL NOT NULL
+- `created_at` TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
+
+## Table `registrations`
+
+- `id` INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT
+- `event_id` INTEGER NOT NULL
+- `student_name` TEXT NOT NULL
+- `college` TEXT NOT NULL
+- `email` TEXT NOT NULL
+- `phone` TEXT NOT NULL
+- `team_name` TEXT NOT NULL
+- `status` TEXT NOT NULL
+- `created_at` TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
+
+## Table `volunteers`
+
+- `id` INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT
+- `event_id` INTEGER NOT NULL
+- `name` TEXT NOT NULL
+- `phone` TEXT NOT NULL
+- `role` TEXT NOT NULL
+- `shift` TEXT NOT NULL
+- `created_at` TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
+
+## Table `sponsors`
+
+- `id` INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT
+- `event_id` INTEGER NOT NULL
+- `company_name` TEXT NOT NULL
+- `contact_person` TEXT NOT NULL
+- `amount` REAL NOT NULL
+- `status` TEXT NOT NULL
+- `created_at` TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
+
+## Data access functions (module chosen by the Database engineer, exported from `database/`)
+
+- `add_event(name: str, category: str, venue: str, date: str, start_time: str, capacity: int, entry_fee: float) -> dict`: Inserts a row with these values and returns the new row as a dict (SELECT * FROM the table WHERE id = lastrowid: always SELECT *, so created_at and the counters come back too). Counters and created_at come from their column defaults.
+- `get_event(event_id: int) -> dict | None`: Returns the row as a dict (SELECT *), or None if the id does not exist.
+- `list_events() -> list[dict]`: Returns every row, as a list of dicts, ordered newest first (ORDER BY id DESC, never ORDER BY created_at: rows added in the same second have the same timestamp).
+- `update_event(event_id: int, name: str, category: str, venue: str, date: str, start_time: str, capacity: int, entry_fee: float) -> dict | None`: Updates the user-entered columns of the row (never counters or created_at) and returns the updated row, or None if the id does not exist.
+- `delete_event(event_id: int) -> bool`: First deletes every row of its children (DELETE FROM registrations WHERE event_id = ?, DELETE FROM volunteers WHERE event_id = ?, DELETE FROM sponsors WHERE event_id = ?; every module's SCHEMA creates all tables), then deletes the row. Returns True if the row existed, else False.
+- `add_registration(event_id: int, student_name: str, college: str, email: str, phone: str, team_name: str, status: str) -> dict`: Inserts a row with these values and returns the new row as a dict (SELECT * FROM the table WHERE id = lastrowid: always SELECT *, so created_at and the counters come back too). Counters and created_at come from their column defaults.
